messages:
Lena Ortiz: Hey folks, quick question about parental leave paperwork. I'm planning to take intermittent leave starting July 2025 (two weeks on, two weeks off) while we finalize childcare. What paperwork do I need to file and how does intermittent impact benefits/pay?

Jordan (People Ops): Congrats Lena. Intermittent leave is fine but we need a leave plan and manager sign-off. Please submit: 1) standard leave request form, 2) intermittent schedule (dates), 3) manager approval email.

Jordan (People Ops): For benefits: while on paid parental leave benefits continue as usual. If you have unpaid intervals, benefits may pause unless you elect to continue coverage and pay employee portion.

Lena Ortiz: Manager is on board. Is there a limit to how many intermittent blocks I can take in a 12-month period?

Jordan (People Ops): We cap intermittent parental leave at 12 weeks total in a rolling 12-month period for the standard policy. If you need more, we can look at accommodations or unpaid leave.

Emma (Finance): Payroll note: intermittent paid leave is processed through the normal payroll run. If you have unpaid blocks that cause year-to-date benefit deductions to change, payroll will reconcile in the next pay cycle. If you want consistent deductions, contact finance for a manual deduction plan.

Benefits Bot: Reminder: submit enrollment/continuation elections within 30 days of the first unpaid block to avoid gaps.

Lena Ortiz: Thanks. Where do I upload the manager approval? HR portal?

Jordan (People Ops): Upload everything to the HR portal under "Leaves" and tag the request "intermittent-parental". I'll link the manager approval to your file after you upload.

Lena Ortiz: Uploaded schedule and manager email. Also tagging for backup on-call coverage — do I need to arrange that before leave?

Jordan (People Ops): Good call. Coordinate with your manager for on-call handoff. We recommend a one-week overlap for knowledge transfer. Also please set your Slack status and update team calendar.

PayrollBot: Note: if intermittent causes partial-paychecks, expect prorated PTO accruals until full-time work resumes.

Lena Ortiz: Great, thanks everyone. I'll monitor benefits and reach out if gaps show up.
